s1.syndrome_frame: Acute vision loss in one eye with optic disc swelling and retinal vascular occlusion in a patient undergoing immunotherapy
salient_findings: Sudden vision loss in the right eye
Marked swelling of the optic disc
Peripapillary retinal hemorrhages and occlusion of the superior branch artery
Combined occlusion of the central retinal artery and vein
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 40s
Undergoing treatment with systemic steroids, durvalumab, and bevacizumab
Initial visual acuity of 20/25 OU
Right eye showed full visual field and relative afferent pupillary defect
Mild swelling of the optic disc on initial examination
Vision loss occurred 10 days after initial presentation
MRI showed focal enhancement along enlarged right optic nerve
Lumbar puncture showed no abnormalities
Vitreous biopsy showed hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm
Immunohistochemistry positive for glial fibrillary acid protein and mutant IDH-1 protein

shortlist.label: arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: optic disc swelling and vision loss in one eye, consistent with ischemic optic neuropathy

shortlist.label: central retinal artery occlusion
shortlist.why_kept: sudden vision loss and lack of perfusion of retinal vasculature on fluorescein angiography

shortlist.label: optic neuritis
shortlist.why_kept: optic disc swelling and vision loss, although less likely given the presence of retinal vascular occlusion

shortlist.label: giant cell arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: optic disc swelling and vision loss in one eye, with potential for arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy

shortlist.label: astrocytic neoplasm
shortlist.why_kept: vitreous biopsy showing hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm, consistent with a rare but possible cause of vision loss

raw.rationale: Vitreous biopsy showed hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm and immunohistochemistry was positive for glial fibrillary acid protein and mutant IDH-1 protein, which strongly supports the diagnosis of an astrocytic neoplasm.

rejected.label: arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy
rejected.why: Lack of evidence for giant cell arteritis and the presence of a hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm on vitreous biopsy

rejected.label: central retinal artery occlusion
rejected.why: While the patient did develop central retinal artery occlusion, it was a secondary event and not the primary cause of the vision loss

rejected.label: optic neuritis
rejected.why: The presence of a hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm on vitreous biopsy and the lack of typical optic neuritis symptoms such as pain on eye movement

rejected.label: giant cell arteritis
rejected.why: Lumbar puncture showed no abnormalities and there is no other evidence to support giant cell arteritis
